Daily Transit Intelligence
June 22, 2026 — 13 papers analyzed
KEY FINDINGS
NYC's congestion pricing program lifted bus and subway ridership well beyond
the tolled zone, while its travel-demand cuts stayed concentrated inside it.
A widely used SUMO mesoscopic traffic model has reportedly underestimated
congestion for two decades due to incomplete queue-spillback physics.
A risk-aware planner remediated a median of 53.6% of transit-desert tracts
across 25 cities within five years, beating static optimization by 5 points.
PAPER OF THE DAY
Revisiting mesoscopic traffic flow simulation in SUMO:
Limitations, analysis, and an alternative
Ying-Chuan Ni, Alina Akopian, Anastasios Kouvelas, Michail A. Makridis
It is the rare infrastructure paper that quietly undermines a swath of prior published
research: SUMO's mesoscopic traffic model, used in countless transit-priority and signal-
timing studies (including several other papers referenced this week), has apparently been
underestimating congestion for two decades due to a flawed treatment of queue spillback. The

ACTIONABLE TAKEAWAYS
Agencies using SUMO mesoscopic simulation for transit-priority or congestion studies should
re-validate key conclusions against the corrected link-transmission model proposed this
week.
Cities considering congestion pricing can now cite a rigorous, uncertainty-aware ridership-
gain estimate from NYC's first year, but should budget for uneven neighborhood-level
adaptation rather than assuming uniform benefit.
Agencies serving immigrant-heavy corridors should prioritize first/last-mile access
investments over fare discounts when the goal is sustaining transit ridership through the
integration process.
Planning departments doing service-change analysis should track the new GTFS 'DayTypes'
formalization as a potential standard for distinguishing real schedule changes from minor
timing shifts.
Transit app teams piloting AI features should look at ChatPlanner's fine-tuning + RAG
combination as a lower-risk way to add preference-aware routing without rebuilding core
trip-planning engines.
